question: A final independent check, motivated by uniform frozen ridge recommendations before inspecting blind test latencies. Can direct prediction of the paired log ratio make useful decisions? Can interpolation on calibrated total work predict absolute latency? The primary test and its thresholds remain fixed.
training: Use only the 32 development graphs and their original three processes. The original 22 blind test graphs and all their timings are excluded. For each requested contract and dominant operator group, collapse chain and branch at each development tier by the median. Interpolate log separate runtime and paired log joint/separate runtime ratio against log work. Outside the training interval extend its end segment for total time (slope clipped to [0,1.5]); hold the boundary ratio constant. Include V0 and sample time as individual targets. Tie selects separate.
features: Source work is main elements plus dense/conv FLOPs and RMS volume. StableHLO work is typed dot and convolution FLOPs, result volumes of arithmetic operations, and separate/variadic reduction domains. Group by convolution, dot, rsqrt, then other. Both estimators receive the requested observation contract and aggregate both development readouts. Also evaluate their equal-weight geometric ensemble, fixed separate, and fixed joint.
test: Eleven additional graphs: affine, dense, RMS and convolution each at two fresh sizes, one chain and one branch; one fresh shape each of gated MLP, Flax basic chain and strided bottleneck. Registered queries: global counts, last-axis counts, squared energies, same-site energy/maximum and a sample. Direct joint only where legal. Five independent processes, 12 interleaved measured rounds after six warmups, four same-executable aliases per implementation, validation seeds 941/2803/7919. Same CPU, timing, legality, correctness and noise floor as the primary study.
decision: Report median and p90 multiplicative errors on observed configurations separately for familiar and held-out architectures, relative to the same 1.30/2.00 targets. Compare runtime and choices with fixed joint. A selection advantage requires graph-clustered 95% interval for geometric mean chosen/joint entirely below one. Report all wins, losses and unresolved changes. This small, predefined last check does not replace primary outcomes.
